Find the position ${s}_{0}$ and velocity ${v}_{0}$ of the particle at the initial moment of time $t=0\,\text{s}.$

${s}_{0}=$
{{field-1}}$\text{m}\,\text{and}\,$

${v}_{0}=$

feedback.problem: The displacement $s$ (in meters) relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by the equation $s(t)=(2t+1)^{3}$, where $t$ is the time, measured in seconds. Find the position and velocity of the particle at the initial moment of time $t=0\,\text{s}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To calculate the initial position, we substitute $t=0$ it into the equation $s(t)=(2t+1)^{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}_{0} & =s(0) \\  & =(2\cdot 0+1)^{3} \\  & ={1}^{3} \\  & =1\,\text{m}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((2t+1)^{3}) \\  & =6(2t+1)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the velocity at $t=0\,\text{s},$ we substitute $t=0$ into the velocity function above:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{0} & =v(0) \\  & =6(2\cdot 0+1)^{2} \\  & =6(1)^{2} \\  & =6\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$
